title: Media stack
description: Jellyfin, the *arr suite and the download clients: what is playing, what the library holds and is missing, what is downloading, and whether the indexers and apps are healthy. Sources: jellyfin-exporter, one exportarr per app, the qBittorrent exporter and the Caddy access log.

panels.title: Status
panels.description: UP = the exporter answers and the app behind it reports healthy. exportarr fails the whole scrape when its app is unreachable; jellyfin-exporter keeps answering but stops reporting jellyfin_up, e.g. on a revoked API key. Either way the tile reads DOWN. NO TARGET = the exporter container itself is gone. Seerr, Questarr and Shelfmark have no exporter; their traffic is in the Health row.

panels.title: Playing now
panels.description: Jellyfin sessions actively playing (paused ones are not counted). Blank = Jellyfin or its exporter is down.

panels.title: Transcoding now
panels.description: Sessions Jellyfin is transcoding rather than direct-playing. These are the ones that load the iGPU/CPU.

panels.title: Download speed
panels.description: SABnzbd + qBittorrent, both through the gluetun VPN tunnel.

panels.title: Arr queue

targets.expr: ((sum(sonarr_queue_total) or vector(0)) + (sum(radarr_queue_total) or vector(0))) and on() (min(up{job=~"sonarr|radarr"}) == 1)

panels.description: Items Sonarr and Radarr are tracking in a download client, including completed ones waiting to import. An item that stays here is usually import-blocked: check the Sonarr/Radarr Activity page.

panels.title: Missing
panels.description: Monitored, released and not on disk: what Sonarr and Radarr are still searching for.

panels.title: Health issues
panels.description: Open System → Health warnings across Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr and Bazarr. 'New update is available' is excluded here (Renovate owns image updates) but still listed in the Health table.

panels.title: Now playing

targets.expr: max by (username, device, type, title, series_title, series_season, series_episode, method) (jellyfin_now_playing_state)
max by (username, device, type, title, series_title, series_season, series_episode, method) (jellyfin_now_playing_progress)
max by (username, device, type, title, series_title, series_season, series_episode, method) (jellyfin_now_playing_remaining)

panels.description: One row per Jellyfin session with an item loaded. Method: directplay = file sent as-is, directstream = remuxed, transcode = re-encoded.

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: Transcoding is a subset of Playing + Paused.

panels.title: Watch time per user, selected range
panels.description: Time spent actively playing, counted in 30 s scrape steps. Paused time is not included.

panels.title: Play method
panels.description: Sessions by how Jellyfin delivers them. A shift toward transcode usually means a new client that cannot decode the library's codecs.

panels.title: Transcode time by reason, selected range
panels.description: Why Jellyfin had to transcode, weighted by how long. ContainerNotSupported / VideoCodecNotSupported point at a client; ContainerBitrateExceedsLimit at a bitrate cap.

panels.title: Jellyfin egress
panels.description: Bytes Jellyfin served, from the Caddy access log. Remote viewers share the home uplink with Kiwix seeding and the relays on Community services.

panels.title: Library
panels.description: Item counts from Jellyfin's /Items/Counts. Types with zero items are hidden.

panels.title: Active transcodes

targets.expr: max by (session_id, username, device, title, container, video_codec, audio_codec, hardware_acceleration) (jellyfin_transcoding_session_info)

panels.description: Per-transcode detail. Hardware acceleration empty = software encode on the CPU. Video copied = only audio or the container is converted, which is cheap.

panels.title: Series
panels.description: Series in Sonarr.

panels.title: Episodes on disk
panels.description: Episode files Sonarr has imported.

panels.title: Missing episodes
panels.description: Monitored, aired, not on disk.

panels.title: Episodes below cutoff
panels.description: On disk, but below the quality profile's cutoff, so Sonarr still upgrades them.

panels.title: Movies
panels.description: Movies in Radarr.

panels.title: Movies on disk
panels.description: Movie files Radarr has imported.

panels.title: Missing movies
panels.description: Monitored, released, not on disk.

panels.title: Library size
panels.description: TV + movie files on disk, as Sonarr and Radarr count them. Music and other libraries are not included.

panels.title: Library size
panels.description: Stacked. Growth is imports; a drop is a deletion or a quality swap to a smaller file.

panels.title: Missing and below cutoff
panels.description: Solid = missing, dashed = on disk but below cutoff. A flat, non-zero missing line means searches are not finding releases: check Prowlarr below.

panels.title: History events per hour
panels.description: Grabs, imports, renames and deletions logged in each app's History, per hour.

panels.title: Movie quality
panels.description: Radarr's movie files by quality. Sonarr's per-episode breakdown is off (it is one API call per series per scrape).

panels.title: Queue
panels.description: Sonarr/Radarr = their tracked download queue. qBittorrent = torrents not yet complete, including Kiwix and manual ones. SABnzbd = jobs in its queue.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Upload below the axis. qBittorrent upload includes Kiwix seeding. All of it rides the ProtonVPN tunnel.

panels.title: Torrents by state
panels.description: stalledUP = complete and seeding with no peer right now, the normal resting state. stalledDL = incomplete with no source: a dead torrent.

panels.title: Incomplete torrents
panels.description: Every torrent below 100 %. ETA 100d = qBittorrent's 'infinity': no seeders reachable.

panels.title: SABnzbd
panels.description: Queue state. PAUSED is either a manual pause or SABnzbd pausing itself, e.g. on a full disk or a provider quota.

panels.title: Usenet provider usage, selected range
panels.description: Bytes fetched per news server. Block accounts only drain when the unlimited providers miss articles, so a growing block bar means the main providers' retention or completion is slipping.

panels.title: Queries per indexer, per hour
panels.description: Searches Prowlarr sent each indexer. The counters start at zero when the exporter starts (no backfill), so the first hour after a restart reads low.

panels.title: Grabs per indexer, selected range
panels.description: Releases actually downloaded via each indexer. An indexer with queries but no grabs is costing API hits for nothing.

panels.title: Indexer health, selected range
panels.description: Failed queries usually mean a Cloudflare challenge FlareSolverr could not pass, a rate limit, or an expired account.

panels.title: Subtitles
panels.description: Wanted = Bazarr is still searching; missing = no subtitle in a language the profile requires.

panels.title: Subtitles by language
panels.description: Subtitle files Bazarr manages, per language.

panels.title: Subtitles by provider
panels.description: Where Bazarr's downloads came from. Only providers from Bazarr's history appear.

panels.title: Health issues

targets.expr: max by (job, type, source, message) ({__name__=~"(sonarr|radarr|prowlarr)_system_health_issues"} == 1) or max by (job, type, source, message) (label_replace(bazarr_system_health_issues == 1, "message", "$1", "issue", "(.+)"))

panels.description: Each app's System → Health list. 'New update is available' is expected here: images are pinned and bumped by Renovate, not by the apps.

panels.title: Free space
panels.description: Free bytes as each app sees its own paths. The media, download and torrent paths share the data pool; Jellyfin's transcode directory sits on the apps NVMe with its config and cache. Jellyfin reports free space per drive, so its library entries would only repeat the media root and are left out.

panels.title: Web UI requests, selected range
panels.description: Requests through Caddy per media vhost, including API calls from apps and clients. Covers the apps without an exporter (Seerr, Questarr, Shelfmark). Per-path detail: App — Detail.

panels.title: Web UI 5xx
panels.description: Server errors Caddy returned per media app, per hour. A 502 burst is the app restarting or down.

panels.title: Exporter scrape duration
panels.description: How long each exporter takes to answer. The scrape timeout is 10 s; exportarr's Sonarr and Bazarr collectors grow with the library size. A jellyfin-exporter collector that fails (jellyfin_scrape_collector_success = 0) does not show here: it shows as DOWN in Status.
